║  2. ZK-Pari batch vs individual verification — BLS12-381             ║

Threads: single-threaded.
Circuit fixed at 2^12 SR1CS constraints (batch cost does not depend on it).
Pool built with the HVZK simulator: statistically indistinguishable
from real proofs, so verification cost is identical by construction.

keygen ... simulating 65536 ... timing ... done

Per-proof cost of individual verification (3 pairings): 711.6 us

2a. Amortised batch cost per proof: us (speedup vs individual)
          N │    wall ms │     us/proof │  speedup
  ──────────┼────────────┼──────────────┼─────────
          1 │        0.7 │       696.38 │     1.0x
        256 │        7.5 │        29.35 │    24.2x
       4096 │       63.9 │        15.59 │    45.6x
      65536 │      734.5 │        11.21 │    63.5x

2b. Where the time goes at N=65536 (ms)
  Phases are re-executed against the public API — the library carries no
  instrumentation — and their total is checked against `batch_verify`.
  challenge │ lagrange │ instance │   T~ MSM │   U~ MSM │   V~ MSM │ pairing │    sum │ measured
  ──────────┼──────────┼──────────┼──────────┼──────────┼──────────┼─────────┼────────┼─────────
       33.8 │     21.4 │      2.2 │    169.8 │    170.3 │    331.1 │    0.58 │  729.2 │    734.5

  T~/U~ are the same MSM over T and U; V~ is the same again but with
  full-width scalars (rho_k * zeta^(k) rather than the 128-bit rho_k).
  The final pairing product is a fixed per-batch cost, which is what
  amortises away.
